title: Operator Lantern — capacity knobs, autoscale policy editor, throughput telemetry & change timeline
text:
Operator Lantern — capacity knobs, autoscale policy editor, throughput telemetry & change timeline

description:
Summary: Build a consolidated Operator Lantern panel in the Console for Dedicated capacity operators that combines: 1) interactive scaling knobs and policy editor for autoscaling and reserved throughput guarantees; 2) per-fleet and per-tenant throughput dashboards with token-level and request-level breakdowns; 3) an editable, queryable change timeline / audit view that surfaces policy edits, rollbacks, and automated scaling events.

Problem: Today operators have to jump between the fleet list, the autoscale studio, and the telemetry explorer to understand why a fleet is throttling or why costs spiked. There is no single-pane workflow to tune policies while immediately validating SLOs against recent traffic patterns, nor is there a clear, compact changelog tied to observable impact (throughput/loss/latency).

Goals:
- Expose core capacity controls (min/max nodes, target RPS, reserved throughput guarantees) with safe defaults and an inline policy simulator.
- Provide an autoscale policy editor that supports time-based overrides, surge protection, and cost-sensitivity sliders.
- Show throughput dashboards with rolling histograms, p50/p95/p99 latency overlays, and per-model token breakdowns for the selected time window.
- Surface a change timeline: manual edits, canary rollouts, automated autoscale decisions, capacity overrides, and operator comments. Each entry links to relevant telemetry and related GitHub PR or runbooks.
- Add RBAC guardrails for who can change guarantees and an audit export for compliance teams.

Design/UX constraints and tradeoffs:
- Inline policy simulator should be lightweight (client-side estimation) and avoid depending on heavy backend runs. We will provide an optional accurate simulation job (async) for longer windows.
- Dashboard sampling must balance fidelity and query cost: default to 1s/10s aggregates but allow admins to un-sample short windows for incident triage.
- Tight coupling between edit and timeline: edits create immutable records but we will allow admins to attach ‘operator rationale’ metadata to help runbooks.

Acceptance criteria:
- Operators can edit min/max capacity, target throughput and apply a policy; changes appear in change timeline with a link to the policy diff.
- Autoscale policy editor supports at least: target RPS, cooldown windows, surge multiplier, cost-sensitivity slider, and scheduled overrides.
- Throughput dashboard displays token counts, request rates, p50/p95/p99 latency, and model mix for the selected fleet over 1h/6h/24h windows.
- Timeline contains entries for manual edits, automated scale events, rollouts, rollbacks, and capacity overrides with timestamps and actor.
- RBAC prevents non-admins from applying guarantees; audit export produces CSV/JSON with >= 90% of timeline fields.

Notes: Link the timeline items to the existing telemetry traces and to the rollout engine to enable one-click rollback when a policy causes degradation.

implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (MVP): knobs UI + policy editor + minimal timeline entries + 1h throughput dashboard (4 weeks). Phase 2: full telemetry rollouts, policy simulator async job, exports, access controls (6 weeks). Phase 3: polish, canary workflows, runbook links (2 weeks).

qa_checklist:
1) Edit policy and verify timeline entry; 2) Apply scheduled override and confirm dashboard shows effective capacity; 3) Trigger autoscale condition in staging and verify automated event recorded; 4) Attempt edit with non-admin role and expect permission denied; 5) Export timeline and validate CSV headers.

observability_criteria:
Dashboard must surface per-route cost and latency deltas within 30s of policy application. Timeline ingestion latency <= 45s for automated events.

notes:
Consider adding integration test that replays a synthetic traffic trace and verifies timeline entries and one-click rollback behavior. Also evaluate cost delta when simulator runs for 24h windows.

comments:
2026-02-25 — Kickoff: PM + ENG + Design sync. Agreed MVP surface: scaling knobs, policy editor, 3 dashboard views, and timeline with export. Action: ENG to prototype policy API contract; Design to ship mocks for knobs and timeline.
2026-03-02 — Design review: Figma v2 accepted with feedback on compact timeline rows. Design added ‘operator rationale’ field to timeline entries. UX request: add quick revert button for last manual change.
2026-03-06 — Eng scoping: Backend work split into policy-api (ENG-84321), telemetry-views (ENG-84609), timeline-store (ENG-84900). Estimated 5 sprints across infra and console teams. Risk: telemetry query cost — will add sampling and pre-aggregates.
2026-03-10 — Security review: scoped RBAC roles and audit export format. Security asked for KMS-backed export for compliance customers (opt-in); added to next milestone.
